title: Level 5 (World Class) - B-15
notes:
West leads the ♦K against 4♠. West's lead of the ♦K marks him with the ♦Q and East with all the remaining high cards for his 1NT opening. South must win as a heart shift from West would immediately sink the contract.

The defense still has communication in diamonds and South has 4 losers. South can go a long way towards solving both of these problems by leading a club from dummy. When East covers, South discards a diamond.

East returns a diamond and South ruffs high. South must now find a way to get to the dummy. The only problem will be when East has all 3 spades. South can guard against this possibility by leading the ♠8 or ♠9 and, when West discards, overtake with the ♠10 in dummy.

East will win (it does him no good to duck) and return the ♠4. South allows dummy to win and plays clubs for heart discards. On dummy's third club winner, East will ruff with the ♠7. South can overruff and cross in trumps to enjoy the rest of the clubs.
